paragraphs: Here's what I love about this passage, friend. The men who were unclean didn't hide, and they didn't shrug and say, "Oh well, maybe next year." They walked up to Moses and Aaron that very day and asked why they should be left out (Numbers 9:6-7). They wanted in, and the LORD made a way for them (Numbers 9:10-11). If you've ever felt like you missed your moment, that's your answer: you bring the question, and you bring it to the right place.

But hold on, because the way in is not a free pass. The later Passover still came with the lamb, the unleavened bread, the bitter herbs, nothing left until morning and not one bone broken (Numbers 9:11-12). A do-over is NOT a discount, friend! Then the LORD says a man who is clean and not on a journey, and still skips it, must be cut off, because he did not present the LORD's offering at its appointed time (Numbers 9:13). The LORD takes His appointed times seriously, and I think a closed door never looked so open to the ones who asked.

And the door doesn't stop at the people you'd expect. A foreigner who wants to observe the Passover to the LORD follows the same statute as the native (Numbers 9:14). Same statute, same invitation. So here's my big idea: when you want to be at the LORD's table, ask Him, do it His way, and don't put it off, because there is room for the one who comes.
